sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Co-localization with LCK-tRFP plasma-membrane marker confirmed; no functional assay of NRAC activity reported.
sites.rationale: The topology landmarks place the C-terminus (residue 160) firmly in the extracellular span (122–160), 39 residues from the TM boundary—well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum. No ledger clip names a specific residue; the N-terminus (1–103) is intracellular (confirmed by L4), making the C-terminus the sole extracellular terminus and the only possible location for this tag. insert_after_residue=160 is therefore topology-derived, not chosen. Python verification confirms seq[159]='L'. Full-length Nrac (C14orf180) cloned into pCMV6-AC-GFP to create a C-terminal GFP fusion (Nrac-GFP); co-transfected with plasma-membrane marker LCK-tRFP in HEK293 cells; fluorescence imaging showed co-localization of Nrac-GFP with the PM marker.

sources.claim: Fluorescence imaging of HEK293 cells transfected with plasmids encoding B) LCK-tRFP and C) Nrac-GFP and D) Merged picture.

literature_notes: All five ledger clips derive from two papers (PMC3459823 and PMC12436663) and describe the same Nrac-GFP C-terminal fusion construct. L1 and L2 describe construct creation; L3 provides the surface-localization result (co-localization with LCK-tRFP); L4 and L5 validate the NRAC antibody using the same NRAC-GFP cells. No ledger clip names a specific insertion residue, so position_evidence is topology_derived. No internal extracellular loop insertions are reported in the ledger. The N-terminal intracellular domain (1–103) is recorded in other_positions. L4 is antibody epitope mapping of the intracellular N-terminus, not a tag insertion, and does not qualify as a surface site.

literature_other_positions.note: L4 explicitly states the N-terminus of NRAC is intracellular ('antibody targeting the intracellular N-terminus of murine NRAC'); topology landmarks confirm residues 1–103 are cytoplasmic, so any N-terminal tag would be intracellular, not a surface tag.
